rules.complete_when: agent branch pushed to origin, or merged into master
rules.m0: dispatch M-0 via --only once P-8..P-12 have all pushed
rules.isolation: content-free checks only; audit via git-visible artifacts
rules.escalation: CLI-unsolvable -> B-* browser-operator session (claude-in-chrome, whitelist, fail-closed) -> needs_human list for the user
rules.provenance: write-as-you-go: run dir created at start, incremental writes per step; context-only info counts as nonexistent
rules.reap: dispatch.py --reap every heartbeat: branch on origin => taskkill the process tree at once; self-exited sessions marked
rules.auditor: A-1 standing drift auditor: reads monitor/AUDITOR.md each cycle, hourly cadence, 6 cycles then exit; heartbeat relaunches if dead; reports in monitor/audit/, silence = healthy; monitor reads reports every heartbeat and adjudicates
rules.quota: quota.py check every heartbeat; limit-signature deaths -> hold (no dispatch, minimal heartbeats); ping (1 haiku call) gates resume; staggered priority relaunch at half pool, runs/ provenance makes restarts lossless
rules.monitor_rebirth: HANDOFF.md rewritten every heartbeat; deep rebirth (re-derive from disk+git, not context) every ~6 heartbeats (~3h); quota death = pause not amnesia, wakeup resumes after ~5h window refresh; a fresh session reading HANDOFF + memory IS the monitor
rules.dispatch_policy: event-driven: (1) per-completion -- a branch merged by M-0 frees its territory, author+dispatch follow-up work consuming the merged outputs at once, freshness beats batching; (2) critical-path preemption -- if WP3 critical path (theoria-arm) is idle or dead, relaunch immediately, jumps every queue; (3) M-0 fires when >=3 delivered-unmerged branches accumulate OR a pending dispatch depends on one; (4) caps: <=10 monitor-dispatched sessions, 2 slots reserved for services (A-1/B-*/M-0); (5) all launches gated by quota mode; recovering = priority list at half pool; (6) backpressure: no new prompt on a territory with a delivered-but-unmerged branch, unless the new work is additive-only in a fresh subdir; (7) staleness: a prompt authored >24h ago re-validates against the tree before launch
rules.frontend_policy: AUTOMATED: TheoriaDashboard scheduled task runs monitor/scan.py every 10 min (pure python, spawns nothing, crash-safe) -- live probes, board, ops heartbeats and the grid refresh themselves. The monitor session only does the judgment layer: spec.py verdicts, PAPER_PLAN percentages, findings, and delivering the page to the user on material change.
rules.stagger: batch dispatch sleeps 45s between launches; storms kill
rules.auto_revive: heartbeat auto-relaunches lost sessions (guard prevents doubles); a prompt lost >=3 times is a suspected prompt-level defect: stop relaunching, escalate as a finding, rewrite or split the prompt before the next attempt
rules.launch_path: one-shot Windows scheduled task per work item (TheoriaAgent-<id>), action = _runner.py <id> (short form; schtasks caps /TR at 261 chars), prompt fed on STDIN (the claude .cmd shim mangles multi-line UTF-8 argv under Task Scheduler -> empty prompt). Detached spawns from the monitor tool shell or from a reflex tick both die; this path survives.
rules.ops_in_app: standing/judgment ops (auditor, browser, merger-judge, retro) run as user app sessions from monitor/prompts/ops/*; dispatch batch refuses A-/B-/M-/R- classes; ci_merge.py stays deterministic-scripted
rules.concurrency: HARD cap after the 2026-07-28 machine crash: reflex keeps at most 2 headless workers alive and refuses to spawn below 8GB free RAM. Ops (4) live in the user app; the monitor itself is an app session. Extra research capacity is added BY THE USER opening monitor/worker.cmd windows -- visible, closable, self-serving from the board.
rules.worker_model: long-lived board workers: claim -> deliver -> claim next; the monitor authors board items and controls headcount only, never per-item dispatch
rules.architecture: SPLIT 2026-07-28: backend = spec.py (judgments) + scan.py (probes) -> state.json, recomputed every 10 min by the TheoriaDashboard task; frontend = monitor/app.html, a pure renderer that fetches state.json every 20s from a local server (monitor/serve.cmd on :8787, TheoriaServe task at logon). The monitor edits backend files locally and the page follows by itself -- no re-delivery, no manual sync. app.html contains zero judgments; scan.py renders zero HTML.
rules.rampup: gradual: first wave 2 headless board workers at 15:20 (after a quota ping); then +2 every ~20 min while free RAM > 8GB, no session deaths, and the board still has claimable items -- ceiling 6 headless (plus 4 ops + monitor in the app). Any death or memory dip freezes the ramp at the current level and reports.
rules.ramp_gate: never add workers while available board items < new workers; supply gates headcount
rules.user_task_routing: 用户交给监控的任务一律下发，不自己做：研究类 → `python monitor/assign.py research <cell> <territory> "<标题>" --id <短名> --body "..."` 落工作板，研究员自助领取；运维类（审计/合并/浏览器/回顾）→ `python monitor/assign.py ops OPS-X "<指令>"` 落邮箱，对应运维下周期读到并回执。监控自己只做三件不可下发的事：判断（spec 裁决/论文口径）、下发本身、以及对 agent 报告的裁决。紧急用 --urgent 置顶。领地冲突在下发时即被工作板挡住。
rules.standing_researchers: ADOPTED 2026-07-28: RES-* standing researchers hold a lane and stay in it (contract monitor/res/<ID>.md, re-read each cycle; heartbeat monitor/ops-status/<ID>.json). Laned board items belong to their lane; generic W-* workers take unlaned items only. Both guards are now two-sided in board.py -- the original leak let a generic worker strip a lane bare.
rules.agent_view: monitor/agents.py renders per-agent plain-language cards on the dashboard from git + board + heartbeats only (isolation contract holds).
rules.commit_hygiene: monitor NEVER uses `git add -A` again: OPS-M caught commit 18384e2 sweeping its half-edited ci_merge.py onto master mid-edit. The monitor commits explicit paths only (spec.py, scan.py, state.json, board/, mailbox/, audit/, HANDOFF, loop_state), and never a file another session may be editing. When in doubt, `git status` first and name the paths.
rules.dispatch_authority: 用户 2026-07-28 授予监控全部 agent 调用权：起停、扩缩、换赛道、改上限、直接下发，一律不必先问。行使原则：供需比驱动（板上可领 > 在跑工人数即扩，反之收）；硬约束只有三条——空闲内存 >8GB、配额窗口开、领地互斥；越界只在两处回到用户：要花的钱超出既有预算闸门，或需要人类身份（登录/付款/验证码）。
rules.scaling_policy: headless workers: reflex keeps up to 7 alive, actual target = min(WORKER_MAX, available board items), gated on >8GB free RAM and quota OPEN; app sessions are never spawned by the monitor (no API), only requested from the user when one dies
rules.spend_authority: 用户 2026-07-28 授权：离线收工即可直接启动烧钱与墙钟的工作，唯一约束是账号额度，其余一律通过。监控据此设额度包并直接下发，不再逐次请示。开发堆战役包 $200 / 单局 $60 / 单次 reserve ≤$25，由 RES-1 独占支用。**监控仍守住的一道门**：封存战役（WP6）在冻结清单提交前不开跑——那不是钱的问题，是主张成立与否的问题，跨门即claim作废；若要提前跨，按既定口径记为一次有意识的例外。
rules.quota_pacing: 账号额度是唯一真约束且为共享池：常驻研究员分批 reserve、每关回报实际花费；监控每次心跳看 spend_gate 账本与 quota 状态，剩余不足时先保 RES-1 的战役线，其余赛道降为纯 token 工作（它们本来就零 API 花费）

notes.permission-wall-root-cause: ALL headless dispatch failures were a permission wall: bypassPermissionsModeAccepted was never set, sessions ran read-only, wrote to scratchpad, exited 0. Fixed: consent flag + settings.local defaultMode + launch via Task Scheduler queue. Death counts reset -- the prompts were innocent. Salvage sweep of dead sessions' scratchpads pending.
notes.permission-verified: synchronous headless probe wrote to the repo at ~1140 local: consent flag + settings.local defaultMode fixed the wall. All prior deaths were the wall, not prompt defects. Full research fleet (11) queued for Task Scheduler launch.
notes.launch-root-causes: three stacked bugs, all fixed 2026-07-28: (1) permission wall (bypassPermissionsModeAccepted never set) -> sessions ran read-only, wrote to scratchpad, exit 0; (2) job-object cleanup killed detached children of the monitor shell and of reflex ticks; (3) UTF-8 argv mangling under Task Scheduler delivered an empty prompt. Verified end-to-end by Z0-permprobe writing to the repo.
notes.machine-crash: 2026-07-28: ~20 concurrent sessions (each running test suites, Lean, FD) exhausted the machine. All TheoriaAgent-* tasks killed, reflex disabled pending the capped rewrite. Peak measured afterwards: 13 claude processes = 2.5GB, so the killer was the work they spawned, not the sessions.

ramp.note: board was empty at 17:22 (0 available, 7 claimed, 6 done) -- authored 4 new items before launching; the bottleneck had moved from headcount to work supply

verify1.decision: STOP at 8 -- all three health signals green, but the board holds only one claimable item. Adding workers now buys BOARD-EMPTY exits, not throughput. Ramp resumes when work supply does.
